reden:
The described issue (H-05) is a chained exploit centered on Stop.stopRent transferring assets (via _reclaimRentedItems delegatecall) before proving the RentalOrder exists, then using the lender’s onERC721/1155Received callback to create a matching order, leveraging EIP-712/signature-binding flaws and the omission of rentalWallet from the rental order hash to make removeRentals succeed—and thereby steal actively rented NFTs and freeze payments. 

The audit content does not describe this specific stopRent-before-validation/callback-based attack path. While the report does identify several constituent bugs used in the chain (e.g., rentalWallet omitted from the order hash; EIP-712/metadata omissions; RentPayload not bound to a specific order), it never ties them to the Stop.stopRent flow nor notes that the order existence check happens only after reclaiming, enabling order creation during the lender’s token-receipt callback. The high-severity items in the audit (fallback handler bypass, disableModule offset) are different vulnerabilities and code paths. 

Because the report does not describe the critical Stop.stopRent sequence (transfer before validation and callback order creation), fixing any single reported issue would not necessarily fix H-05; the report did not detect the same vulnerability.
